# Hub v2 V4: the Assets area, Add asset, and records the master applies with Undo

Step 4 of 7 of Hub v2. Needs V1. Read PROJECT-BRIEF.md first, then the head comments of `hub/assets.js`. No model call anywhere in this step's code. Hub files and `assets-register.json` only.

## Goal
Assets is its own area with six stages: Wanted, Received, Staged, Converted, In game, Credited. The owner adds an asset with a form. When the owner tells the master "we are adding assets", the master's record lines update Assets at once, with Undo. Record changes cost no press; anything else still does.

## Build
1. `hub/assets.js`: add the hand-set stage `staged` (the file is in `assets-src/`, named and ready to convert) between `received` and `converted`. Add the worked-out flag `credited` (in game AND it has a credit and a licence, by the same check that feeds the existing credit-gap list). Keep the rule that a register entry may not claim `converted` or `in-game`: the dist modules decide those. `retired` stays, shown folded.
2. `hub/records.js` (pure) and `hub/records-store.mjs`: a record change is `{id, at, by: 'you'|'master', op: 'asset-add'|'asset-stage', before, after}` appended to `.hub/records.jsonl`. `applyRecord(register, change)` and `undoRecord(register, change)` are pure; undo is refused (409) when the row changed after the record. `assets-register.json` is written with temp file then rename, no BOM, its key order and indentation kept so the diff stays small.
3. Routes (hub token, POST + JSON + same Origin, 64 KB): `POST /api/assets/add {name, kind, source, licence, stage, note}` (name 1 to 80 characters, kind from the existing list, stage one of wanted, received, staged, source an http or https link or empty, no file paths); `POST /api/assets/stage {id, stage}` (only between wanted, received, staged and retired); `POST /api/records/undo {id}`; `GET /api/assets/summary` (counts per stage, new files in `assets-src/` not matched to a row, the last 10 records). These work without `--runs`.
4. Assets page in the shell (`#assets`): the "Next step" line; a strip of the six stage counts, the three hand-set ones marked; the Add asset form; rows grouped by stage with a stage pill, "Move to" for the hand-set stages, and Undo on rows changed by a record; "New file: <name>. Which asset is it?" with the closest row names offered (matched by name by script); links to the existing pictures page (`/assets`) and the 3D viewer. Cards obey the 560 px rule.
5. Master: a reply may carry lines of the form `RECORD: asset add name="..." kind=... stage=wanted source=...` and `RECORD: asset stage <id> <stage>`, at most 6 per reply, above any PLAN: section. `hub/chat.js` parses them strictly (same limits as the routes; anything else is ignored and shown as "not understood"), applies them at once through the same code as the routes with `by: 'master'`, and stores the change ids on the message; the chat page shows "Recorded: <name> → <stage>" with Undo. `hub/status.js` adds the stage counts and unmatched new files to the status block. `MASTER_RULES` explains RECORD: and says it is for records only: anything that costs tokens, writes game files or starts a run stays an ACTION the owner presses.
6. Tests: `tests/hub-records.mjs` (apply, undo, 409 on a changed row, register formatting is stable, strict parsing with hostile input, the cap of 6) and server tests (token, limits, a stage the register may not claim is refused). Fake CLI: a `master` reply with RECORD lines. Add an Assets screenshot to `scripts/hub-shots.mjs`.

## Rules
- Do not change `dist/`. Do not touch files in `assets-src/` (read names only).
- No BOM. Run `npm test` after each change; finish with `npm run index`, then `npm test`. Stop with tests passing; report failures honestly. Do not commit.

## Done when
The form and the master both add rows and move stages at once, every such change can be undone, worked-out stages cannot be set by hand, and tests cover each refusal.
